period_note: Year-end position from the Annual Report 2024's own 'Five-Year at a Glance' summary table (audited), CONSOLIDATED basis. Reporting basis is now EXPLICITLY CONFIRMED (previously inferred from magnitude only): Note 14.a.2.1 'CRAR as defined by the Basel Capital Accord (Consolidated)' reports Total Regulatory Capital BDT 37,013.20m for 2024, which reproduces exactly in the Five-Year at a Glance table's 'Total Regulatory Capital' row; the Segment Report's explicit 'Consolidated' column (Annexure G-i) gives Total Assets BDT 457,203.99m, again matching the Five-Year at a Glance row exactly, while its explicit 'Solo' column gives BDT 454,310.97m, matching Annexure F(i) 'Financial Highlights on the Overall Activities (Solo)' exactly. All three independently confirm the multi-year table used for this and prior years' extraction is Consolidated, not Solo. Credit Metrics (classified loans, NPL%, coverage) are explicitly labelled '(SOLO)' within the same Five-Year at a Glance table -- numerically basis-invariant in practice since only the parent bank (not subsidiaries MTBSL/MTBCL) extends loans, confirmed by identical classified-loan and provision figures appearing in both the FY2023 report's Solo (Annexure F(i)) and Consolidated (Annexure F) tables. npl_pct (6.95%) reproduces exactly from classified_loans (20,740.44) / SOLO gross loans (298,506.91) = 6.95%; dividing by this record's own CONSOLIDATED gross_loans (300,780) instead gives 6.90%, a 0.05pp difference consistent with the credit-quality section being Solo within an otherwise Consolidated record. provision_classified (10,563) is Annexure F(i)'s 'Total Provision Maintained against Classified Loans' (Solo-labelled, basis-invariant per above) -- the same concept as the FY2011-2023 field, continuing that series' coverage trend (49.85% FY2023 -> 50.93% FY2024, see provision_coverage_classified_only_pct). gross_npl_coverage_pct is a DIFFERENT, broader metric starting this report: the FY2024 table's own 'NPL/Loan Loss Coverage Ratio' (96.66%) sums general + off-balance-sheet + margin-loan + classified provisions over classified loans, not classified-provision-only as in FY2011-2023's 'Gross NPL Coverage' -- a methodology break in the source document itself, not this dataset; provision_coverage_classified_only_pct is added alongside it to preserve comparability with the pre-2024 series. ldr_pct is newly added from the source's own reported 'Advance-Deposit Ratio (As per BB Asset-Liability guideline)' (76.76%) -- this is NOT the same as naive gross_loans/total_deposits (300,780/328,837=91.47%); this dataset's ratios_timeseries.json has historically computed a 'calculated' LDR as that naive ratio for FY2015-2023 (e.g. 99.41% for FY2023), which diverges materially from MTB's own regulatory ADR for the same year (84.19% per the FY2023 report) -- a pre-existing methodology quirk in the already-stored 2015-2023 series, flagged here (not corrected retroactively, out of this task's scope). cet1_capital is newly split out from tier1_capital: Note 14.a.2.1 discloses Additional Tier-1 capital (a BDT 4,000m perpetual bond) separately from CET-I for both FY2024 and its FY2023 comparative; MTB's own FY2023 annual report's 'Five Years at a Glance' table appears to have folded this AT1 into its printed 'Common Equity Tier-I' figure (23,799) without separating it, meaning the already-stored 2023_Q4.json 'tier1_capital' field (value 23,799, labelled 'Common Equity Tier-I Capital') is actually TOTAL Tier-1 (CET1 19,799 + AT1 4,000) per this report's restated 2023 comparative, not pure CET1 as its own original label claims -- flagged here as a cross-report label inconsistency found during cross-validation; 2023_Q4.json is NOT modified (Tier1+Tier2=Total Regulatory Capital still holds for it either way). DISCREPANCY vs already-stored 2023 data (not corrected, 2023_Q4.json left untouched): this report's FY2023 comparative column shows Total Assets (Consolidated) BDT 366,606m and (Solo) BDT 364,086m, versus BDT 369,327m (Consolidated, per 2023_Q4.json) / BDT 366,808m (Solo) in the FY2023 report's own contemporaneous figures -- a BDT ~2,721m (0.74%) reduction applied near-identically to both bases (369,327-366,606=2,721; 366,808-364,086=2,721), suggesting a common reclassification between the two report vintages; the FY2023 P&L (interest income/expense) reproduces unchanged in this report's comparative column, so only the FY2023 balance-sheet total-assets figure moved. profit_before_tax/tax_expense/profit_after_tax and operating_income use FY2024's OWN figures per this report (Segment Report Annexure G-ii, Consolidated column) -- the FY2025 report's later comparative column for FY2024 shows a reclassification between Interest Expense (BDT 17,601m there vs 18,968m here) and Non-Interest Income (BDT 14,444m there vs 15,811m here), a BDT 1,367m shift each way that leaves Total Operating Income (22,509m) and Profit Before Tax unchanged both ways; per the standing rule this dataset keeps the contemporaneous FY2024 figures (18,968m interest expense, 15,811m non-interest income, 6,698m NII), not the FY2025 report's restated view.
